protocol.name: cutefish_window_management_v1

description.summary: task list and window control for cutefish-shell

protocol.description:
Lets the trusted Cutefish shell enumerate and control the ordinary application windows the compositor manages, which is what the dock's task list, the status bar and the launcher are built on.
Only ordinary application windows are announced. The shell's own cutefish_shell_v1 surfaces - the desktop, the panels, the launcher and the notification banners - are never part of this list. Ordinary toplevels whose app_id is exactly cutefish-shell are also excluded.
Every request here is a trusted shell command. Unlike xdg-activation or xdg_toplevel.move they carry no input serial: the shell acts on behalf of the user through its own UI, not on behalf of the target application.
The compositor only advertises this global to the one trusted shell client it was handed by the session. Ordinary applications never see it.
Warning! Not a standard protocol. Backward-incompatible changes are made by bumping the interface version.

interface.name: cutefish_window_management_v1

description.summary: the managed window list

interface.description: On bind the compositor announces every application window that already exists, each one followed by its state and a done event, and then keeps sending changes. Rebinding after a shell restart therefore repopulates the whole task list.

description.summary: what is shown at a picked position

entry.name: none
entry.summary: nothing that can be captured as a window

entry.name: panel
entry.summary: a shell panel such as the status bar

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop managing windows

request.description: Existing cutefish_window_v1 objects stay valid until destroyed.

request.name: quit_application

description.summary: the application menu's Quit

request.description: Asks every top-level window of the window's application to close, as xdg_toplevel.close does; dialogs are left alone, so a second Quit asks again rather than dismissing a prompt. An application is the task-list windows of one app_id, as the dock groups them, or of one process for windows without an app_id. Their processes that have no task-list window left a few seconds later are terminated through the session's application runtime; one that still shows a window, typically to ask about unsaved changes, is not.

request.name: hide_application

description.summary: the application menu's Hide

request.description: Hides every window of the window's application, as cutefish_window_v1.hide does.

request.name: hide_other_applications

description.summary: the application menu's Hide Others

request.description: Hides the windows of every application but the window's; with no window, of every application.

request.name: pick

description.summary: find the window shown at a position

request.description: Asks which window is shown at a position in global logical coordinates, found the way the pointer finds it but looking through screen capture surfaces and their popups, so the capture interface can pick what is under it. Answered by picked with the same serial.

request.name: activate_desk

description.summary: switch to a desk

request.description: Slides to the desk as clicking it does. Ignored for a desk that no longer exists and while desks are being switched.

request.name: create_desk

description.summary: add a desk after the last one

request.description: Ignored when there are as many desks as the compositor allows. With `activate` 1 the new desk is also switched to.

request.name: remove_desk

description.summary: remove a desk, keeping its windows

request.description: The desk's windows go to the desk on its left, or on its right when it is the first, below that desk's own windows. Removing the active desk slides to that desk first. Ignored for the only desk.

request.name: set_desk_name

description.summary: name a desk

request.description: An empty name gives the desk its default name back.

request.name: create_surface_capture_source

description.summary: a capture source of the shell's own window as it is shown

request.description: Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 of the window one of the shell's own surfaces produced, with what the compositor draws around it: the glass, the outline, the shadow and the transparent margins the shadow needs, so a still picture of the dock looks the way the dock does on screen. The buffer covers the shadow bounds of what casts the shadow - the rounded body of the dock, not the transparent room of its surface around it - at the scale of the output that holds most of the window. A surface that has no window yet gives a source that cannot be captured. In every other way the source behaves like the one cutefish_window_v1.create_capture_source gives.

event.name: window

description.summary: a window appeared

event.description:
A new cutefish_window_v1 object for an application window. Its state follows immediately, terminated by cutefish_window_v1.done.
`id_hi` and `id_lo` are the high and low 32 bits of the compositor's stable 64-bit window identifier. Wayland has no 64-bit scalar, so the identifier is carried as two uints; it is unique for the lifetime of the compositor and is never reused.
The same window's ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1 identifier is "cutefish-" followed by this identifier in decimal, so a capture client can be told which window to capture.

event.name: active_window

description.summary: the active window changed

event.description: The identifier of the active managed application, or zero when no application is active. An ordinary cutefish-shell toplevel taking keyboard focus preserves the previous managed application context.

event.name: initial_state_done

description.summary: the initial enumeration is complete

event.description: Sent once, after the windows that existed at bind time have all been announced. A shell that is rebuilding its task list can hold off drawing until this arrives.

event.name: picked

description.summary: the window shown at a picked position

event.description: The answer to pick. For a window, id_hi and id_lo name it, and a popup is answered with the window it belongs to; otherwise they are zero.

event.name: desk

description.summary: a desk was added

event.description: Desks are announced in order, before initial_state_done for those that exist at bind time; a new desk is always the last. `desk` is its identifier, unique for the lifetime of the compositor and never reused, and never zero.

event.name: desk_removed

description.summary: a desk was removed

event.description: Its windows have moved to another desk, which their desk events say.

event.name: desk_name

description.summary: a desk's name

event.description: Empty while the desk has its default name, which the shell words itself from the desk's position, as "Desk 2".

event.name: active_desk

description.summary: the desk in front of the user

event.description: There is always one.

interface.name: cutefish_window_v1

description.summary: one managed application window

interface.description: State arrives as individual events followed by done. The shell should apply a batch only when done is received.

description.summary: stop tracking this window

request.name: activate

description.summary: raise the window and give it the keyboard focus

request.description: Unhides the window first if it is hidden, and restores it if it is minimized.

request.name: close

description.summary: ask the application to close the window

request.description: Sends the ordinary xdg_toplevel.close; the application decides what to do about it. A window that is not responsive gets not_responding instead.

request.name: start_move

description.summary: begin an interactive move of this window

request.description: Used by the status bar's window menu. No input serial is required.

request.name: set_minimized_geometry

description.summary: where the window minimizes to

request.description:
The rectangle, in the coordinate space of `panel`, that this window's task-list entry occupies. The compositor uses it as the target of the minimize animation. `panel` must be a surface belonging to the same client.
Passing a zero-sized rectangle clears the association.

request.name: handoff

description.summary: the dock now shows the minimized window

request.description: Answers minimize_landed. Send it once the panel surface has committed a frame that shows the window's thumbnail at its minimized geometry; the compositor then stops drawing the window there. Ignored when no landing is pending.

request.name: hide

description.summary: take the window off the screen without minimizing it

request.description:
The window disappears at once: no animation, no thumbnail, and no task-list slot to land on. Its state is kept underneath, so a minimized window stays minimized and comes back to the dock when it is unhidden. A hidden window cannot be activated; if it held the keyboard focus, the focus moves on as it does for a closed window.
cutefish_window_management_v1.hide_application and hide_other_applications apply it to whole applications.

request.name: unhide

description.summary: show a hidden window again

request.description: The window reappears in the state it was hidden in, in place and with no animation. It is neither raised nor activated; send activate for that. Ignored when the window is not hidden.

request.name: move_to_desk

description.summary: send the window to a desk

request.description: Its dialogs go with it. Zero puts it on every desk. A window on the active desk slides off towards the desk it goes to, and does not take the user along.

request.name: force_quit

description.summary: end the application behind the window

request.description: Ends the client process at once, without asking it: what the shell offers once not_responding was sent. When the session started the process in an application scope of its own, the rest of that scope ends with it. Anything the application did not save is lost.

request.name: create_capture_source

description.summary: a capture source of the window as it is shown

request.description: Creates an ext_image_capture_source_v1 of the window with what the compositor draws around it: the outline, the shadow and the transparent margins the shadow needs, so a still picture of the window looks the way the window does on screen. The buffer covers the window's shadow bounds instead of its bounds, at the scale of the output that holds most of the window; a window that fills its area casts no shadow and gives the same picture as the toplevel source. In every other way the source behaves like one from ext_foreign_toplevel_image_capture_source_manager_v1.

event.name: pid

description.summary: the process that owns the window

event.description: Taken from the Wayland client credentials of the connection the window's xdg_surface was created on, or for an X11 window from the credentials the X server holds for its client connection. Never from a client-supplied property such as _NET_WM_PID. Zero when unknown.

event.name: state

description.summary: the window's boolean state

event.description: Each argument is 1 or 0. `hidden` is independent of the others: a window can be both hidden and minimized.

description.summary: the outer window bounds in global coordinates

event.name: done

description.summary: the end of a batch of state changes

event.description: Everything sent since the previous done applies atomically.

event.name: closed

description.summary: the window is gone

event.description: No further events are sent. The shell should destroy the object.

event.name: application_menu

description.summary: the window's DBusMenu endpoint

event.description: Service and object path of a com.canonical.dbusmenu on the session bus. Empty strings clear the endpoint. Applies with the next done event.

event.name: thumbnail

description.summary: how the window looked when it was minimized

event.description:
Sent once the window is minimized: the last frame the compositor presented for it, outline and shadow excluded, for the shell to show in the window's place. Also sent during the initial enumeration for windows that are already minimized.
May be replaced while minimizing. Before minimize_landed, the final thumbnail contains the same raster the compositor holds at the slot. Upload it unchanged to preserve its edge pixels and sampling at handoff.
`fd` is a read-only shared memory file of width * height * 4 bytes, rows top to bottom, in the byte order of wl_shm format argb8888 with premultiplied alpha. The shell maps it, copies what it needs and closes it. No thumbnail is sent to clear one: the image stops applying once the state event reports the window as no longer minimized. Applies with the next done event.

event.name: minimize_landed

description.summary: the minimize animation reached the dock

event.description: The window has arrived at its minimized geometry, without shadow or outline, and the compositor keeps drawing it there until the shell sends handoff, or for at most 250 ms. Showing the thumbnail and then sending handoff replaces the window with no frame in between.

event.name: parent

description.summary: the window this one is transient for

event.description: The identifier of the xdg_toplevel parent, or zero when the window stands on its own. A dialog such as a save prompt has a parent; the shell leaves those alone when it asks an application to quit, since closing the prompt would answer it on the user's behalf. Applies with the next done event.

event.name: skip_taskbar

description.summary: effective application presentation exclusion

event.description: When set, omit this window from the dock, status bar application identity and window switcher. It remains managed and may receive focus. Apply this state together with the other events at done.

event.name: desk

description.summary: the desk the window is on

event.description: Zero for a window on every desk: one the user put there, an always on top window or a system dialog. A window on a desk that is not active is not on screen, and activating it switches to its desk. Applies with the next done event.

event.name: responsive

description.summary: whether the application answers the compositor

event.description: Zero once the client stopped answering the compositor's pings past a timeout, one when it answers again. The compositor dims the window meanwhile. Every window starts out responsive. Applies with the next done event.

event.name: not_responding

description.summary: the user is waiting on a window that stopped answering

event.description: Sent when the user presses on, types into or closes the window while it is not responsive. The shell is expected to offer force_quit. With no shell bound to offer it, closing such a window ends the application instead.
